parent.title: Decision framework: which React i18n library to adopt in 2026

siblings.title: React i18n in 2026: The Core Library Head-to-Head
siblings.summary: react-i18next is still the safe default; next-intl owns the Next.js App Router; Paraglide and Lingui are the compile-time challengers worth betting on.

siblings.title: Message format, pluralization & ICU across React i18n libraries (2026)
siblings.summary: ICU-first (react-intl, next-intl, Lingui) vs interpolation-first (i18next default, typesafe-i18n) vs MF2-inspired (Paraglide) — how each authors plurals, gender and Intl-formatted numbers/dates.

siblings.title: React i18n in 2026: framework & runtime fit (React 19, RSC, Vite vs Next.js)
siblings.summary: next-intl or Lingui for the Next.js App Router; Paraglide or react-i18next for a Vite SPA — the split is compile-time (tree-shakeable) vs runtime-dictionary architecture.

siblings.title: React i18n 2026: the translation pipeline, not just the library
siblings.summary: The i18n library you pick decides your extraction model and file format, but the TMS you pair it with decides your actual workflow — here's how the couplings line up in 2026.

sources.title: i18next — TypeScript
sources.claim: i18next achieves type safety via module augmentation of CustomTypeOptions with a declared resources type; v25.4+ adds enableSelector for better IDE performance.

sources.title: react-i18next — TypeScript
sources.claim: react-i18next documents a d.ts declaration file augmenting i18next with defaultNS and resources to type the t() function.

sources.title: auto18n — React i18n 2026
sources.claim: react-i18next TypeScript support requires a separate declaration file and is less ergonomic than react-intl; Lingui co-locates messages but needs an SWC/Babel build plugin.

sources.title: Lingui — Message Extraction
sources.claim: Lingui extracts messages via static analysis of t/Trans macros using lingui extract; cannot extract from variables, and supports dependency-tree crawling for per-page catalogs.

sources.title: Lingui vs react-intl
sources.claim: Lingui provides a CLI that extracts and merges messages with existing translations, supporting Babel and SWC, versus react-intl needing manual merge.

sources.title: js-lingui (GitHub)
sources.claim: js-lingui is a readable, automated, optimized 2kb i18n library with CLI, Vite plugin, and ESLint plugin.

sources.title: paraglide-js (GitHub)
sources.claim: Paraglide JS is a compiler-based i18n library emitting tree-shakable typed message functions, up to 70% smaller bundles.

sources.title: Paraglide vs react-i18next
sources.claim: Paraglide types keys and parameters by default so a renamed or missing message is a compile error, versus react-i18next's opt-in augmentation you maintain.

sources.title: inlang — Paraglide JS
sources.claim: Paraglide compiles messages into typed ESM functions enabling Vite tree-shaking and TypeScript autocomplete of keys and parameters; plugin-based message format (ICU or i18next/JSON).

sources.title: typesafe-i18n (GitHub)
sources.claim: typesafe-i18n is a zero-dependency, fully type-safe i18n library whose generator outputs TypeScript definitions and wrappers from the base locale.

sources.title: typesafe-i18n — docs
sources.claim: typesafe-i18n runs a generator that creates boilerplate wrappers in development mode for full type safety.

sources.title: next-intl — TypeScript workflow
sources.claim: next-intl generates a .d.json.ts declaration via createMessagesDeclaration to strictly type message keys against the default locale.

sources.title: next-intl 4.0
sources.claim: next-intl 4.0 lets you declare a Locale type in AppConfig so useLocale() and Link pick up the app-specific locale type.

sources.title: next-intl — VSCode integration
sources.claim: next-intl documents official VSCode integration for its i18n workflow.

sources.title: i18n Ally (GitHub)
sources.claim: i18n Ally is an all-in-one i18n VS Code extension supporting inline annotations and missing-key management across many frameworks including i18next, react-intl, and Lingui.

sources.title: i18n Ally — Configurations
sources.claim: i18n Ally shows translations as inline annotations, offers one-click translate of missing/stale keys, and stale-translation detection via regex key/usage matching.

sources.title: React Intl | FormatJS
sources.claim: react-intl (FormatJS) provides runtime ICU message formatting for React.

sources.title: FormatJS — Message Declaration
sources.claim: FormatJS uses defineMessages returning Record<string, MessageDescriptor> as the hook for CLI, Babel, and TS plugins to extract and type messages.

sources.title: FormatJS — CLI
sources.claim: FormatJS CLI extracts from defineMessages/FormattedMessage with hash-based ID interpolation and offers a verify command with --missing-keys and --extra-keys for completeness.

sources.title: dev.to — Best i18n libraries 2026
sources.claim: 2026 comparison rates typesafe-i18n best-in-class type safety, Paraglide/next-intl fully typed with autocomplete, react-intl and react-i18next only 'good' with manual setup.

sources.title: simplelocalize — Popular React localization libraries
sources.claim: 2026 rankings: next-intl full key autocompletion without codegen; Paraglide/typesafe-i18n compile-time codegen with parameter-level checks; Lingui macro extraction 'genuinely fast'.

sources.title: formatjs (GitHub)
sources.claim: FormatJS is the monorepo behind react-intl and the @formatjs/cli extraction tooling.

sources.title: i18next (GitHub)
sources.claim: i18next is the core internationalization framework underpinning react-i18next.

sources.title: next-intl (GitHub)
sources.claim: next-intl is a Next.js-focused i18n library with typed messages and navigation APIs.

sources.title: lingual.dev — type-safe translation keys
sources.claim: The recommended react-i18next path uses i18next-resources-for-ts to auto-generate resource types from JSON before augmentation.

sources.title: formatjs #1677 — Better defineMessages typings
sources.claim: react-intl message-id type safety needs global FormatjsIntl namespace override; typed defineMessages remains a long-standing feature request.
